rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse groups Jews, Christians, and polytheists in resentment of Muslims, then distinguishes Jewish-Christian disputes; polytheists are worst for obstructing worship at the sanctuary and sharing hostility to Islam.
rows.anchor: ثم قرن اليهود والنصارى والمشركون في قرن حسدهم المسلمين والسخط على الشريعة الجديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion turns to the sanctuary, Abraham and his prayer for descendants, Islam as Abrahamic monotheism, the Kaaba's qibla and Meccan rites; Judaism and Christianity are not Abraham's religion.
rows.anchor: وانتقل بهذه المناسبة إلى فضائل المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The change of qibla rebuts the People of the Book; purifying souls matters more than facing east or west, and replacing earlier laws with what benefits later peoples is no novelty.
rows.anchor: وأن العناية بتزكية النفوس أجدر من العناية باستقبال الجهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument returns to creation, the disavowal of leaders on Judgment Day, and food prohibitions, ending with people who do not profess Islam but display affection toward Muslims.
rows.anchor: ثم عاد إلى محاجة المشركين بالاستدلال بآثار صنعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse begins a new utterance, syntactically independent of the disjoint letters alif-lam-mim, on the most apparent analysis.
rows.anchor: مبدأ كلام لا اتصال له في الإعراب بحروف

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: On the view that alif-lam-mim is a challenge, the demonstrative may point to those letters: the book is composed from the Arabs' own letters, yet they cannot rival it.
rows.anchor: صاحب ( الكشاف ) على احتمال أن تكون حروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the apparent reading, the demonstrative is the subject, al-kitab is an appositive explaining the unseen referent, and what follows supplies the predicate; the reference is the Quran already revealed.
rows.anchor: وعلى الأظهر تكون الإشارة إلى القرآن المعروف لديهم يومئذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative can refer to the revealed Quran known then, meaning the surahs preceding al-Baqara, since every portion already revealed is called Quran and later revelation joins it.
rows.anchor: النازل بالفعل وهي السور المتقدمة على سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it refers to the whole Quran, including future revelation, which is mentally anticipated; al-kitab then explains the demonstrative and لا ريب فيه is the predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الإشارة إلى جميع القرآن ما نزل منه وما سينزل

rows.speaker: الرضي
rows.claim: Al-Radi says demonstratives are for present, near objects, while distant forms can point to absent things; near forms are less common for absent referents, with the pattern reversed for speech.
rows.anchor: وضع اسم الإشارة للحضور والقربب لأنه للمشار إليه حسا

rows.speaker: ابن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik allows near and distant demonstratives alike for preceding discourse; Ibn Ashur says his account better matches actual usage and rejects al-Radi's broad claim of rarity.
rows.anchor: وابن مالك في ( التسهيل ) سوى بين الإتيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation between distant and near demonstratives for one referent appears across the Jesus passage, where 3:58 and 3:62 point to the same account.
rows.anchor: إن هذا لهو القصص الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both demonstrative distances also occur for a non-speech referent, as in the two men whom Moses found fighting: one is of his party and one his enemy.
rows.anchor: فوجد فيها رجلين يقتتلان هذا من شيعته وهذا من عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because both forms are linguistically available, eloquent speakers select between them for contextual purposes; here the distant form elevates the Quran's rank and makes it seem remote in dignity.
rows.anchor: فلا جرم أن كانت الإشارة في الآية باستعمال اسم الإشارة للبعيد لإظهار رفعة شأن هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noble thing is figuratively placed high and out of reach to protect it from wear and casual handling; the Quran is likewise beyond the polytheists' ability to rival it.
rows.anchor: وقد شاع في الكلام البليغ تمثيل الأمر الشريف بالشيء المرفوع في عزة المنال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran may be distant because its truthful meanings and beneficial guidance are beyond those who dismiss it as fabricated or tales of the ancients.
rows.anchor: أو لأنه لصدق معانيه ونفع إرشاده بعيد عمن يتناوله بهجر القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nearby demonstrative in 6:92 is no objection: it points to a book physically before its audience to encourage study and heedfulness.
rows.anchor: فذلك للإشارة إلى كتاب بين يدي أهله لترغيبهم في العكوف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari apparently did not treat the distant demonstrative as an honorific; Ibn Ashur praises the author of al-Miftah for listing distance as a means of glorification.
rows.anchor: ولعل صاحب ( الكشاف ) بنى على مثل ما بنى عليه الرضي

rows.speaker: خفاف بن ندبة
rows.claim: Khuffaf's line uses ذلك to present himself as a figure of elevated standing, illustrating the honorific force of a distant demonstrative.
rows.anchor: كما قال خفاف بن ندبة : أقول له والرمح يأطر

rows.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
rows.claim: Qays ibn al-Khatim uses the near demonstrative هذا for death to convey disregard, illustrating a contextual use of proximity.
rows.anchor: كقول قيس بن الخطيم في ( الحماسة ) : متى يأتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitab may be an appositive to the demonstrative, identifying its unseen referent by definite reference; the clause لا ريب فيه then serves as predicate.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون بدلا من اسم الإشارة لقصد بيان المشار إليه لعدم مشاهدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively al-kitab is the predicate, and its definite article marks the genus; defining both terms rhetorically restricts complete bookhood to the Quran, not by literal exclusion of other books.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( الكتاب ) خبرا عن اسم الإشارة ويكون التعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The genus reading means the Quran gathers the perfect qualities of books, while other scriptures lack some such perfection; grammarians call this definite article a marker of perfection.
rows.anchor: ذلك هو الكتاب الجامع لصفات الكمال في جنس الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab means something written: it can be an intensive verbal noun or a fa'al form with passive sense, like libas for something worn.
rows.anchor: و ( الكتاب ) فعال بمعنى المكتوب إما مصدر كاتب المصوغ للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root كتب means to gather and join, since a book gathers its pages and letters.
rows.anchor: واشتقاقه من كتب بمعنى جمع وضم لأن الكتاب تجمع أوراقه وحروفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet ordered all revelation to be written and appointed scribes; calling the Quran a book signals writing as its preservation, and Quranic writing is a communal obligation.
rows.anchor: فإن النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم أمر بكتابة كل ما ينزل من الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا ريب فيه may be a circumstantial phrase modifying al-kitab or one of its first or second predicates, as already discussed.
rows.anchor: حال من الكتاب أو خبر أول أو ثان على ما مر قريبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayb means doubt, but originally denotes inner anxiety and disturbance; calamities of time are also called rayb because they unsettle the soul.
rows.anchor: والريب الشك وأصل الريب القلق واضطراب النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs رابه and أرابه both mean to make someone doubt; the hamza does not add causative force, like the pairs لحق وألحق and زلقه وأزلقه.
rows.anchor: ويقال أرابه كذلك إذ الهمزة لم تكسبه تعدية زائدة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes the verbs: أراب is weaker than راب and means bringing someone close to doubt.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل إن أراب أضعف من راب أراب بمعنى قربه من أن يشك قاله أبو زيد

rows.speaker: بشار
rows.claim: Bashshar's verse witnesses the distinction, using أرِبتُ for being brought near to doubt.
rows.anchor: قال بشار : أخوك الذي إن ربته قال إنما

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The hadith advises leaving an action that makes one uncertain about its prohibition for another whose permissibility is clear; Ibn Ashur gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك )

rows.speaker: القراء المتواترون
rows.claim: The transmitted readers all pronounce لا ريب with fatḥ, negating the genus emphatically; nominative رفع could deny only an individual doubt rather than all doubt.
rows.anchor: في فتح { لا ريب } نفيا للجنس على سبيل التنصيص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the demonstrative points to the challenge in alif-lam-mim and al-kitab predicates it, no doubt specifically denies uncertainty that a book made from familiar letters could defeat them.
rows.anchor: نفيا لريب خاص وهو الريب الذي يعرض في كون هذا الكتاب مؤلفا من حروف كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majority attach فيه to rayb as an adverbial complement and pause there, as in the cited verses; alternatively it is a stable predicate for هدى.
rows.anchor: ظرفا مستقرا خبرا لقوله بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second parse, figurative containment means the Quran's wording indicates guidance; the indefinite هدى suggests some guidance and coaxes avoidant hearers to listen.
rows.anchor: هو الظرفية المجازية العرفية تشبيها لدلالة اللفظ باحتواء الظرف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr, إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية, an example of figurative containment; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قول النبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم لأبي ذر : ( إنك امرؤ فيك جاهلية )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of لا is omitted because it is obvious—there is no doubt present; this omission is common, as in قالوا لا ضير and ordinary لا بأس.
rows.anchor: محذوفا لظهوره أي لا ريب موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possible sense is guidance for future people who will become God-fearing; the verbal noun هدى itself carries no fixed tense.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه هدى في المستقبل للذين سيتقون في المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Quran هدى, rather than هاد, conveys richer praise and leads into praise of believers who benefit from its guidance.
rows.anchor: حصل من وصف الكتاب بالمصدر من وفرة المعاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides the pious in religion, public affairs, ethics, legislation, and jurisprudence across ranks and times, according to their effort, learning, and needs.
rows.anchor: ومن منتفع في السياسة وتدبير أمور الأمة

rows.speaker: أئمة الأصول
rows.claim: Legal theorists count jurisprudential ijtihad as taqwa and infer its obligation from the command to fear God as much as one can.
rows.anchor: وقد جعل أئمة الأصول الاجتهاد في الفقه من التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Any failure to benefit fully reflects a shortcoming in the recipient, not a defect in Quranic guidance; scholars and the pious keep striving to follow it more completely.
rows.anchor: فإنما ذلك لنقص فيه لا في الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four opening clauses cohere: alif-lam-mim announces inimitability; ذلك الكتاب praises the Quran's perfection, urging rational Arabs to follow and take pride in it, and reminding the People of the Book it surpasses their scripture.
rows.anchor: تسجيل لإعجاز القرآن وإنحاء على عامة المشركين عجزهم عن معارضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين يؤمنون connects to للمتقين as an adjective that elaborates the general description and begins a digression classifying four kinds of Quran recipients.
rows.anchor: على أنه صفة لإرداف صفتهم الإجمالية بتفصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the Hijra people fell into believers and open disbelievers; afterward hypocrites and People of the Book formed two additional groups, joining forces against Islam when it arose in Medina.
rows.anchor: هما المنافقون وأهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praised muttaqin here are former polytheists who embraced Islam; the relative clause at 2:4 introduces a second believing group.
rows.anchor: فريق هم المتقون الذين أسلموا ممن كانوا مشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These converts were moved by taqwa and concern for their ultimate fate, unlike Musaylima, who came with Banu Hanifa concealing hostility and seeking rule; Wa'il ibn Hujr came seeking Islam.
rows.anchor: فوائل بن حجر مثلا لما جاء من اليمن راغبا في الإسلام هو من المتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their new faith in the unseen means belief after formerly denying resurrection and the afterlife, as the Quran recounts in many verses.
rows.anchor: أي بعد أن كانوا يكفرون بالبعث والمعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three present-tense descriptions signal renewed, ongoing belief, prayer, and spending, qualities these converts acquired only after Quranic guidance reached them.
rows.anchor: اجتلبت في الإخبار عنهم بهذه الصلات الثلاث صيغة المضارع الدالة على التجدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns hypocrites drawn from Yathrib, Jews who displayed Islam, and Bedouin living nearby.
rows.anchor: والآية أشارت إلى طائفة من الكفار وهم المنافقون الذين كان بعضهم من أهل يثرب

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: A report from Ka'b ibn Malik says that more than eighty hypocrites stayed behind from the Tabuk expedition; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: ورد في حديث كعب بن مالك أن المنافقين الذين تخلفوا في غزوة تبوك بضعة وثمانون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Named hypocrites include Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, their leader, and al-Jadd ibn Qays; the passage also lists others from varied groups.
rows.anchor: وقد عرف من أسمائهم عبد الله بن أبي بن سلول وهو رأس المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jallas ibn Suwayd is linked to the revelation of the verse about people swearing by God that they did not say something.
rows.anchor: والجلاس بن سويد الذي نزل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source also names the Jewish Abd Allah ibn Saba and Labid ibn al-A'sam, an ally of the Jews from Banu Zurayq, citing al-Bukhari's medicine chapter on sorcery.
rows.anchor: وعبد الله بن سبأ اليهودي ولبيد بن الأعصم من بني زريق حليف اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi outwardly displayed affection and faith; Ibn Ashur says his case will be discussed under 2:204.
rows.anchor: والأخنس أبي بن شريق الثقفي كان يظهر الود والإيمان وسيأتي عند قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn al-Lusayt and Wadi'a ibn Thabit discouraged Muslims from Tabuk; some said Zayd repented and improved, while others denied it. Mikhshan ibn Humayr repented, was forgiven, and died a martyr at Yamama.
rows.anchor: وزيد بن اللصيت القينقاعي ووديعة بن ثابت من بني عمرو بن عوف

rows.speaker: ابن حزم
rows.claim: Ibn Hazm classed Mu'tab ibn Qushayr among hypocrites; Ibn Ashur rejects this because Mu'tab fought at Badr, though his remark at Uhud showed weak faith.
rows.anchor: لابن حزم قد ذكر قوم معتب بن قشير الأوسي

rows.speaker: الزبير بن العوام
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam transmitted Mu'tab's Uhud remark that, had they controlled events, they would not have died there; Ibn Atiyya says Mu'tab was suspected of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: رواه عنه الزبير بن العوام قال ابن عطية كان مغموصا بالنفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Afak's hypocrisy appeared after the Prophet killed al-Harith ibn Suwayd; Abu Afak composed an insinuating poem, was ordered killed, and Salim ibn Umayr killed him.
rows.anchor: ظهر نفاقه حين قتل رسول الله الحارث بن سويد بن صامت وقال شعرا يعرض بالنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asma bint Marwan became hypocritical after Abu Afak's death and composed an insinuating poem; Umayr ibn Adi al-Khatmi killed her, and the Prophet said, لا ينتطح فيها عنزان.
rows.anchor: ومن المنافقات عصماء بنت مروان من بني أمية بنن زيد نافقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bashir ibn Ubayriq is described as a hypocrite who satirized the Prophet's companions and fought at Uhud; Tha'laba ibn Hatib is also listed, though he had become Muslim and was counted among Badr's people.
rows.anchor: كان منافقا يهجو أصحاب رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another Ansari hypocrite refused a Jew's request to let the Prophet judge their dispute and sought Ka'b al-Ashraf instead; Umar killed him, and the incident is linked to the verse in al-Nisa'.
rows.anchor: فدعا اليهودي بشرا إلى حكم النبيء فامتنع بشر وطلب المحاكمة إلى كعب بن الأشرف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that in the Prophet's time the hypocrites numbered three hundred men and one hundred seventy women.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المنافقين على عهد رسول الله كانوا ثلاثمائة من الرجال ومائة وسبعين من النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Aws and Khazraj, Abd Allah ibn Ubayy organized hypocrisy out of resentment: Yathrib had agreed to make him king after Bu'ath killed many leaders, but Islam frustrated that plan.
rows.anchor: فالذي سن لهم النفاق وجمعهم عليه هو عبد الله بن أبى حسدا وحنقا على الإسلام

rows.speaker: سعد بن عبادة
rows.claim: In a report in al-Bukhari, Sa'd ibn Ubadah urged the Prophet to pardon Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, explaining that Yathrib had been ready to crown him and he resented losing that position; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: قال سعد بن عبادة للنبيء في حديث البخاري : اعف عنه يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing believers and their opponents, the passage begins an address suited to every group, extending guidance and mercy despite their misconduct.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي ثني به العنان إلى موعظة كل فريق من الفرق الأربع المتقدم ذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general address reassures people after threats and blame: divine severity aims at reform, like a mentor who rebukes then gently restores the pupil's spirits.
rows.anchor: ففيه تأنيس لأنفسهم بعد أن هددهم ولامهم وذم صنعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consolation increases the good in the righteous and turns wrongdoers from misconduct, so each previously described group receives its share of the address.
rows.anchor: الإقبال على موعظة نبذ الشرك وذلك هو غالب اصطلاح القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Quranic usage, O people chiefly introduces an exhortation to abandon polytheism; the prohibition of rivals in 2:22 confirms the aim, and the vocative dignifies the address.
rows.anchor: قوله : { فلا تجعلوا لله أندادا وأنتم تعلمون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يا is the most frequent vocative particle and the default form; when a vocative particle is omitted, no other one is implicitly supplied.
rows.anchor: حرف للنداء وهو أكثر حروف النداء استعمالا فهو أصل حروف النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Legislative addresses are not limited like ordinary speech to whoever is physically present; hearers are directly obligated, while later generations receive the address as information, analogously to legal theory on commands.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن خطابات التشريع ونحوها غير جارية على المعروف في توجه الخطاب في أصل اللغات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship originally means abasement and submission; Ibn Ashur had discussed the term under 1:5.
rows.anchor: عند قوله تعالى : { إياك نعبد } ( الفاتحة : 5 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True submission requires certainty, so belief in God and exclusive divine unity are the beginning of worship; associating an unworthy partner undermines submission to God.
rows.anchor: ولما كان التذلل والخضوع إنما يحصل عن صدق اليقين كان الإيمان بالله وتوحيده بالإلاهية مبدأ العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes Arab polytheists, materialists, People of the Book, and believers, each according to their duty: affirm the Creator, God's unity, the Messenger, Islam, and continued obedience.
rows.anchor: فالمخاطب بالأمر بالعبادة المشركون من العرب والدهريون منهم وأهل الكتاب والمؤمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared command is the common meaning of worship across audiences, avoiding polysemy for those who reject it; Ibn Ashur allows polysemy when context supports it, and 2:22 branches from the command.
rows.anchor: فالمأمورية هو القدر المشترك حتى لا يلزم استعمال المشترك في معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse does not prove that unbelievers are addressed by subsidiary legal duties: for them worship means faith, monotheism, and affirming the Messenger, which is agreed upon.
rows.anchor: فليس في هذه الآية حجة للقول بخطاب الكفار بفروع الشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meaning of Lord was explained under al-Fatiha 1:2.
rows.anchor: عند قوله تعالى : { الحمد لله رب العالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using your Lord instead of another identifying form signals that the one who manages creation's affairs especially deserves worship, which expresses gratitude and dependence.
rows.anchor: ووجه العدول عن غير طريق الإضافة من طرق التعريف نحو العلمية إذ لم يقل اعبدوا الله
